segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly I tell you, there are some of those standing here who will certainly not taste death until they see that the kingdom of God has come in power.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After six days Jesus took Peter, James, and John with him and led them up a high mountain, privately, by themselves. And he was transformed in front of them,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and his clothes became dazzling, intensely white, as no launderer on earth could whiten them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter spoke up and said to Jesus,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Rabbi, it is good that we are here. Let us make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For he did not know what to say, because they had become terrified.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then a cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came from the cloud:

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: “This is my beloved Son; listen to him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Suddenly, when they looked around, they no longer saw anyone with them but Jesus alone.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As they were coming down from the mountain, he ordered them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They kept the matter to themselves, debating what this rising from the dead meant.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they asked him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Elijah does come first and restores all things. How then is it written about the Son of Man that he must suffer much and be treated with contempt?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But I tell you that Elijah has in fact come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written about him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they came to the disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and scribes debating with them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At once the whole crowd, when they saw him, were utterly amazed, and they ran up and greeted him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He asked them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What are you debating with them?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Someone from the crowd answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, I brought my son to you. He has a mute spirit,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams at the mouth and grinds his teeth and goes rigid. I asked your disciples to cast it out, and they were not able to.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You unbelieving generation! How long am I to be with you? How long am I to put up with you? Bring him to me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They brought the boy to him. When the spirit saw Jesus, it immediately threw the boy into convulsions, and he fell to the ground and rolled about, foaming at the mouth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus asked his father,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “How long has this been happening to him?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Since childhood.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: It has often thrown him even into fire and into water to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “‘If you can’! All things are possible for the one who believes.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Immediately the child’s father cried out,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I believe; help my unbelief!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Jesus saw that a crowd was rapidly gathering, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You mute and deaf spirit, I command you: come out of him and never enter him again.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After crying out and convulsing him violently, it came out. The boy became like a dead body, so that most of them were saying that he had died.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him, and he stood up.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he had gone into a house, his disciples asked him privately,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Why could we not cast it out?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “This kind can come out by nothing except prayer.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They went on from there and were passing through Galilee, and he did not want anyone to know it,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for he was teaching his disciples and telling them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The Son of Man is being handed over into human hands, and they will kill him, and after he is killed, he will rise after three days.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they did not understand the saying, and they were afraid to ask him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They came to Capernaum. When he was in the house, he asked them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What were you discussing on the way?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they were silent, for on the way they had argued with one another about who was the greatest.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He sat down, called the Twelve, and said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If anyone wants to be first, that person must be last of all and servant of all.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he took a little child and stood the child in their midst, and taking the child in his arms, he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes not me but the one who sent me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: John said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he was not following us.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do not stop him, for there is no one who will do a deed of power in my name and soon afterward be able to speak evil of me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For whoever is not against us is for us.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink because you belong to Christ—truly I tell you, that person will certainly not lose their reward.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for that person to have a great millstone hung around the neck and to be thrown into the sea.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life maimed than to have two hands and go away into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into Gehenna.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into Gehenna,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For everyone will be salted with fire.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Salt is good; but if the salt loses its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”

notes.note: Jesus does not say which event he means. Proposals include the transformation on the mountain that follows immediately, the resurrection, the coming of the Spirit, and the fall of Jerusalem in the year 70; others take the saying as expecting the end within a generation. The Greek tense pictures the kingdom as already arrived when it is seen.

The Greek verb is the ordinary word for a change of form, the same one usually translated “be transformed” in Romans 12:2 and 2 Corinthians 3:18. “Transfigured” comes from the Latin translation and survives in English almost only as a name for this event, which is why most versions keep it. The meaning is not in dispute.

The word is the plain Greek for a tent. The Greek Old Testament uses it both for Israel’s wilderness sanctuary and for the huts of the Feast of Booths, and either echo may be heard here. Older versions have “tabernacles”; modern ones vary among “tents”, “shelters” and “dwellings”.

The scribes’ teaching rests on Malachi 4:5–6, which promises that Elijah will be sent before the day of the Lord. Jesus’ reply points to John the Baptist, whose execution Mark has already told in chapter 6; Matthew’s parallel says so outright. Which Scripture is meant by “as it is written about him” is uncertain, though many point to the persecution of Elijah by Ahab and Jezebel in 1 Kings 19.

Jesus picks up the father’s own words from the previous verse; the Greek marks them as a quotation. Many later manuscripts add “believe”, giving the reading familiar from the King James Version, “If you can believe, all things are possible”. The shorter text has the earliest support and is followed by nearly all modern editions.

Most manuscripts read “prayer and fasting”, as in the King James Version. The words “and fasting” are missing from a few of the earliest witnesses, and most modern editions judge them an early addition reflecting church practice. The manuscript support for the longer reading is nonetheless broad.

The verb is the ordinary Greek word for transferring someone into another’s power, and Mark uses it in turn for what Judas, the chief priests and Pilate each do to Jesus. “Betrayed”, found in some versions, names a treachery the context may supply but the word itself does not state. The Greek also plays on “Son of Man” and “hands of men”, which “human hands” partly preserves.

The Greek word is the ordinary word for power, here used of a single act that displays it. “Miracle” is an accurate rendering and the meaning is not disputed. “Deed of power” is chosen so that the link with “power” elsewhere, as in verse 1, stays visible.

notes.phrase: causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble
notes.note: In the Greek Old Testament the related noun is used for a snare or obstacle, and the verb means to bring about someone’s fall in loyalty to God. The King James “offend” now suggests hurt feelings, and “cause to sin”, used in some modern versions, is narrower than the Greek. Several current translations also have “cause to stumble”.
Literally “a donkey millstone”: the heavy upper stone of a mill turned by a donkey, as distinct from the small hand mill used in a household.

Gehenna is a place name, the Valley of Hinnom beside Jerusalem, which the Old Testament associates with child sacrifice (Jeremiah 7:31–32) and which by Jesus’ time had become a name for the place of final judgment. Most translations render it “hell”, usually with a footnote giving the name. The name is kept here because “hell” merges it with Hades and with later imagery.

notes.phrase: their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched
notes.note: The words echo the last verse of Isaiah (66:24), which pictures the corpses of those who rebelled against God. Many later manuscripts repeat this sentence after verses 43 and 45, where the King James tradition numbers it as verses 44 and 46. The earliest witnesses have it only here, so modern editions omit those two verses and the numbering skips them.

notes.phrase: everyone will be salted with fire
notes.note: Many manuscripts add “and every sacrifice will be salted with salt”, drawing on Leviticus 2:13; the short form translated here has the earliest support and is generally preferred. The saying itself is obscure. It is commonly read either of the fire of judgment just mentioned or of a purifying trial that disciples must undergo, and the question remains open.

candidates.reason: Occurs in both transfiguration accounts and in Romans 12:2 and 2 Corinthians 3:18; the parallels should agree on “transformed” or “transfigured”.
Very frequent in the Gospels and Acts, and translators divide among “scribe”, “teacher of the law” and “legal expert”; readers would be confused by variation.
Recurs in the receiving-a-child and mission sayings across the Synoptics, where versions split between “receive” and “welcome”.
The standard exorcism verb throughout the Gospels and Acts; “cast out” and “drive out” are both common and should not alternate between chapters.
The negative of the register’s πίστις family (with ἄπιστος, v. 19); “unbelief”, “lack of faith” and “faithless” need aligning with believe/faith across books.
